overview: The Medford City Council met to address several municipal matters, including setting the fiscal year 2026 property tax rates and continuing discussions on the Salem Street zoning corridor amendment. The council also approved a six-year police union contract, passed a resolution regarding a controversial proposal to reduce trash collection frequency, and ordained a new tree committee.

items.title: Approval of Records
items.summary: The council approved the records of the November 12th, 2025 meeting.

items.title: Condolences for George Sacco
items.summary: The council approved a resolution expressing condolences on the passing of former School Committee member and State Representative George Sacco.

items.title: Police Patrol and Superiors Wage Adjustments
items.summary: The council waived the three readings and approved a six-year collective bargaining agreement featuring cost-of-living adjustments and body camera implementation provisions.

items.title: Raza's Grill Common Victuals License Amendment
items.summary: The council approved an amendment to extend Raza's Grill's operating hours to 1 a.m. daily, subject to a 30, 60, and 90-day review.

items.title: National Grid Grants of Location
items.summary: The council approved two petitions for grants of location to install updated SCADA monitoring cabinets at Bradbury Avenue and Ross Street.

items.title: Salem Street Corridor Rezoning Map Change
items.summary: The council voted to continue the public hearing on the Salem Street zoning map amendment to December 2nd while awaiting a formal, public commitment from the mayor to fund community engagement for the broader zoning overhaul.

items.title: FY 2026 Property Tax Classification
items.summary: The council adopted the maximum allowable commercial tax shift factor of 0.905494, while voting not to adopt residential or small commercial exemptions. The council also approved scheduling a Committee of the Whole meeting to explore funding to support the future implementation of a residential exemption.

items.title: Zero Waste Initiative Trash Collection Resolution
items.summary: The council approved an amended resolution requesting reports, a public forum, and rodent mitigation plans from the administration following the announcement that trash collection would be reduced to biweekly in July 2027.

items.title: Tree Committee Ordinance
items.summary: The council waived the three readings and ordained an ordinance establishing a volunteer tree committee to assist the tree warden and protect the municipal tree canopy.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents spoke regarding Veterans Day celebrations, local ICE activity, and clarified the operational and financial differences between composting programs and biweekly trash schedules.
